target.statement: SLEID achieves F1 = 96.80% (and precision 97.86%, recall 95.78%, accuracy 99.44%) for illicit account detection, outperforming supervised and semi-supervised baselines
target.dataset: Custom Ethereum DeFi dataset (581 curated illicit seeds expanded to 44,675 core addresses / 1,888,553 accounts, 6,903,860 transactions, 2015-2024)

compute.basis: The headline number depends on a bespoke dataset built by crawling Ethereum (Etherscan/DeFi) from 581 manually curated illicit seeds, expanding via network neighbors, and computing ~100 graph/temporal/transaction/neighborhood features over 1.9M accounts; no code or data is released, so the entire data-construction and feature pipeline would have to be rebuilt before any RF/XGBoost training (which itself is cheap).

blockers: No code released (no repository link in paper)
No dataset released; requires re-crawling Ethereum via Etherscan/DeFi APIs and manual curation of 581 illicit seeds
Labeling protocol (risk-score <0.2, DeFi-priority expansion) is only partially specified and not reproducible exactly
Feature extraction over 1.9M accounts / 6.9M transactions is heavy and depends on external blockchain data services
title: Leveraging Ensemble-Based Semi-Supervised Learning for Illicit Account Detection in Ethereum DeFi Transactions
